To use the direct object pronouns: lo, la, los, las (it, him, her, them).
To use the indirect object pronouns: me, te, le, nos, os, les (to me, to you, to him…).
To combine them: me lo, te la, SE lo (it to me, it to you, it to him).
To put the pronouns in the right place: before the verb or attached to the infinitive.

Pronouns attached to the verb aren’t pronounced separately: regalarle = “re-ga-LAR-le”, envuélvamelos = “en-BWEL-ba-me-los”. The stress stays on the verb’s syllable.
They are pronounced together, like a single word: “selo”, “sela”: Se lo doy = “selo-DOY”.
1. The direct object: lo, la, los, las
To avoid repeating a thing or a person, you replace it with a pronoun, as in English: “The book? I bought IT.”
And for people: me (me), te (you), nos (us), os (you, plural).
Do you know Mihai? — Yes, I know him.
In English every thing is “it”, but in Spanish you choose by the noun’s gender! “La cartera” (the wallet, feminine) → LA compré; “el libro” → LO compré.
2. The indirect object: le, les (to him, to them)
The indirect object answers “to whom?”: “I give A BOOK (direct) TO MY MOTHER (indirect).”
I gave my mother a scarf.
Spanish often doubles it: “LE regalé una bufanda A MI MADRE” = literally “I gave TO HER a scarf TO MY MOTHER”. Pronoun + name. It’s normal and correct!
3. Both together: me lo, te la, SE lo
When you have both pronouns, the indirect one (to whom) comes first, then the direct one (what): “me lo” = it to me.
The special rule: LE and LES become SE before lo / la / los / las. You never say “le lo”!
The book for your mother? I’ll give it to her tomorrow.
The presents for your parents? I’ll send them to them.
Remember: “le lo” sounds awkward (le-lo-le-lo), so Spaniards turned it into “se lo”.
ATTACHED to the infinitive (or before the conjugated verb)
When you attach two pronouns, the verb usually gets a written accent so the stress doesn’t move: da → dámelo, envuelva → envuélvamelos.
Could you gift-wrap it for me?
Thank you so much, I love it!

Ana explains one of Spain’s loveliest traditions to Mihai.
In Spain, children don’t only get presents at Christmas.
The most important presents are brought to them by the Three Kings, on the night of 5 January.
Beforehand, the children write them a letter. In the letter they ask them for toys and books.
On the afternoon of 5 January there is a parade in every town.
The Kings ride through the streets and throw sweets to the children.
In the evening, the children leave their shoes in the living room.
They also leave water and food for the camels. They’re very tired after the journey!
In the morning, next to the shoes, they find the presents.
If a child hasn’t behaved well, the Kings leave them coal… but it’s sugar coal!
On that day, families eat roscón de Reyes, a sweet with a surprise inside.
Whoever finds it is king or queen for the day.
Mihai, this year you’re going to write them a letter too. And I’ll give it to them!

The birthday of Elena, Pablo’s wife, was on Friday. Pablo wanted to give her something special.
Elena had told him many times that she really liked some earrings in a jeweller’s in the centre.
Pablo went to the jeweller’s on Thursday afternoon. He found them straight away, and the assistant wrapped them for him in gold paper.
On the way out, he ran into his sister Lucía. “What have you got there?”, she asked him.
“Elena’s present. But don’t tell anyone,” he answered.
Lucía also had a bag with a gold package: it was a cookbook for her friend Inés.
They both went into a café, put their bags on the table and talked for an hour.
When they left, each of them took a bag… but not their own.
On Friday evening, Pablo gave Elena the present with a big smile.
Elena opened it slowly. Inside was a book: “A hundred recipes for stress-free cooking”.
Elena looked at Pablo. Pablo looked at the book. There was a terrible silence.
“Are you telling me I’m a bad cook?”, she asked.
At that moment Pablo’s phone rang. It was Lucía: “Pablo, I think I’ve got your earrings… Inés has just opened her present!”.
Pablo explained everything to Elena. At first she didn’t believe him, but then she laughed so hard she cried.
An hour later, Lucía came with the earrings. Elena put them on straight away.
“They’re gorgeous,” she said. “But I’m keeping the book. That way Pablo will cook more often.”
Inés, for her part, got the cookbook a week later and laughed a lot about the whole story.
Since then, Pablo buys presents on his own.
¿Qué hace Elena con el libro al final?
